Guidance anchor: Minimum eight ANC contacts, with the first contact in the first trimester up to 12 weeks.
Relevant Notebook 4 signals: Early ANC initiation; ANC4+ to ANC8+ continuation
Programme relevance: Provides the national standard against which timing and continuity gaps can be reviewed.
Interpretation boundary: Notebook 4 measures observed attainment patterns, not compliance of individual facilities with the guideline.

Guidance anchor: ANC programme implementation should address equity, quality, standardization, demand and utilization.
Programme relevance: Supports examining whether ANC access and continuity differ across population and geographic contexts.
Interpretation boundary: Observed subgroup differences do not identify the specific health-system mechanism responsible.

Source: WHO Recommendations on Antenatal Care for a Positive Pregnancy Experience (2016)
Guidance anchor: ANC should provide a minimum of eight contacts and the first contact should occur within the first 12 weeks of gestation.
Programme relevance: Supports treating both timely initiation and sustained contact as distinct programme-review dimensions.
Interpretation boundary: WHO recommendations provide programme standards; Notebook 4 does not estimate the causal effect of meeting those standards.

Guidance anchor: Countries may adapt ANC delivery to context, including care through trained providers at facilities or through community outreach services.
Relevant Notebook 4 signals: Travel time; wealth; regional access patterns
Programme relevance: Provides an evidence-based basis for reviewing alternative service-delivery arrangements where repeated travel burden is substantial.
Interpretation boundary: Notebook 4 cannot determine which delivery model would be effective in a particular region or woreda.

Guidance anchor: Group ANC and community-based communication/support approaches require attention to context, women's preferences, trained facilitators, infrastructure and implementation resources.
Programme relevance: These approaches may be considered as review options where local evidence suggests access, communication or continuity barriers.
Interpretation boundary: Group ANC should not be presented as a proven solution from Notebook 4; WHO implementation guidance includes important context and research considerations.

Source: WHO community mobilization guidance for maternal and newborn health
Guidance anchor: Community participation and women's-group approaches can support maternal and newborn health, community support and use of skilled care.
Relevant Notebook 4 signals: Early initiation; religion/context; regional entry gaps
Programme relevance: Supports investigating community-level engagement where ANC entry or timely initiation is weak.
Interpretation boundary: Applicability should be assessed locally and should not be inferred directly from subgroup associations.
